scope: New exact rational curvature certificate for g(E) and exact endpoint signs on I=[13.61,24.58] eV, conditional on fixed numerical J.
question_before_first_run: Does the actual HeIII scalar kernel have strictly positive second derivative over all I? This is a hypothesis until the exact domain certificate succeeds.
arithmetic: fractions.Fraction; source binary64 reals and serialized J decimals as exact rational inputs
derivative_strategy: Eliminate positive sigma and opacity/J factors from g''; derive a polynomial numerator in z=sqrt(E/(E0 ya)); compare two symbolic polynomial derivative routes exactly.
domain_strategy: Exact rational enclosure z in [49/50,33/25], which contains the compact diagnostic energy interval.
curvature_sign_strategy: Try the whole enclosure in Bernstein basis. If not all coefficients are strictly positive, preserve the attempt and bisect dyadically, with maximum depth 8 fixed in advance. Only complete positive coverage establishes strict convexity; an unresolved leaf is a certificate failure, never a physical sign conclusion.
endpoint_strategy: Enclose each exact endpoint z with adjacent multiples of 10^-18 using integer sqrt; require strict polynomial signs across each enclosure using exact Bernstein coefficients.
success_criterion: Every frozen-input, denominator/domain, symbolic identity, basis conversion, complete positive coverage, and endpoint-sign check passes.
failure_policy: Preserve the first code bytes, output, stdout, stderr and execution receipt. Do not loosen signs, endpoints, arithmetic or subdivision limits silently. Any follow-up correction requires a new named evidence path and stated reason.
provenance: Polynomial add/multiply/differentiate/affine/Bernstein utility algorithms adapted from the frozen PHYS23 exact sign helper by reading its source. No import or execution of an inherited main or proof suite.
